intro:
The Ice March

February 23rd, 1918

Rostov is ours as of this morning: empty barracks, a burning quartermaster's store, and a city that had hung out red cloth before our patrols were through the outskirts. The Volunteer Army walked out of it in the dark and took every pair of felt boots in the town with it.

Four years ago I was an officer of the Imperial Army, and a good many of the men I once messed with are in the column now crawling south across the frozen steppe. Alekseyev and Kornilov have taken everything that will march - their staffs, their cadets, their wounded, their families - and they have gone off the railway on purpose, into open country where our armoured trains cannot follow.

The Military Revolutionary Committee has not ordered me to chase them into the snow. Whatever that column becomes, it becomes it somewhere else. My orders are to close the Don behind it - the crossings and the stanitsas it is using - so that nothing of theirs can turn back on Rostov or reach Novocherkassk from the south.

Victory conditions:
- Take Rostov (19,17), Aksaiskaya (26,16) and Ol'ginskaya (29,20).
- The Volunteer column wins instead if four of its formations reach Kraskynova (38,32).

briliant.text:
Rostov, Aksaiskaya and Ol'ginskaya are in Soviet hands and the lower Don is shut. The task the Committee set me has been carried out.

The column itself is gone into the Kuban. I will not pretend otherwise, and I will not write in my report that we destroyed it: we had neither the cavalry nor the fodder to hold open steppe in February, and no one who has seen that country in a thaw would promise it. What we have done is take away its base. Kornilov marches now with what he carries, and every stanitsa behind him belongs to the Soviets.

They will be back. Whatever they gather in the Kuban, they will have to come back through these same crossings, and we shall be standing on them.

That is the whole of it. The Kuban will now have to fight the battle we should have finished on the Don.

intro:
Tragedy at Ekaterinodar

April 9th, 1918

Kornilov has perhaps six thousand men. There are three times that in and around Ekaterinodar, and he is going to attack anyway, because our detachments hold every railway in the Kuban and the Rada's own ministers are sitting in our jails. He can attack or he can starve on the steppe.

He will not try the front of the city. Our scouts have found a crossing being prepared to the west, at Elizabetinskaya - a flanking march in the old style, with Cossack guides who know the fords. Which means the city has to be held on two faces at once, and the village of Takhtamukay across the river, where his column forms up, has to be taken away from him.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Ekaterinodar (17,7) and Elizabetinskaya (5,10).
- Take Takhtamukay (20,19).

briliant.text:
Ekaterinodar has held. On the fourth morning of the assault a shell came through the wall of the farmhouse at Elizabetinskaya where Kornilov had his headquarters, and killed him where he stood. Denikin took over what was left and broke off the attack that night.

They buried him somewhere on the road and ploughed the ground over the grave so we would not find it. We found it.

Their army is not destroyed - it is going back to the Don, where Krasnov's Cossacks have risen and the German divisions in Ukraine will sell them anything they can pay for. But the Kuban is Soviet, and the man they called the soul of the whole affair is dead.

intro:
Belaya Glina

June 28th, 1918

Denikin has come back into the Kuban, and this time his people are not refugees: nine thousand men, German rifles bought through Krasnov's Don government, and the whole of the Don behind him.

We are the Red Army of the North Caucasus and we are on our own. Moscow has the Germans on the Ukrainian line and the Czechoslovak revolt on the Volga; nothing is coming from the north. Five days ago they took Torgovaya and cut the railway to Tsaritsyn, and an army larger than theirs on paper is now an army with no telegraph, no supply and no orders except the ones we write ourselves.

My sector is the line itself. Belaya Glina, Novopokrovskaya and Peschanokopskoye are junctions: while we sit on them this army still has a spine. Their forward depot has halted north of us, and I intend to take it off them.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Belaya Glina (14,6), Novopokrovskaya (4,7) and Peschanokopskoye (21,7).
- Take their supply line at (24,1).

briliant.text:
The three junctions are still ours and their forward depot is a field of burnt tarpaulins. General Markov was killed by one of our shells at Shablievka a few days back, and the Officers' Regiment that carries his name went into our wire twice today and came out thinner both times.

The task was to keep the line open, and the line is open. Further south, though, Tikhoretskaya is being turned, and an army that cannot be told what to do by wire cannot hold a front three hundred versts wide. We are going to have to shorten it.

intro:
The battle for Ekaterinodar

August 13th, 1918

My dear Katya,

You will read in the papers that the Kuban is holding. It is holding here, in front of me, on a line I could walk before breakfast.

Tikhoretskaya has gone, Armavir is threatened, and Denikin has brought up everything he has for the capital of the Kuban. His army has grown - half the stanitsas have gone over to him - and I can tell you exactly how far ahead of him the news travels, because I have been reading the reports out of the districts he has already taken. The land goes back to the man who owned it in 1916. The ataman comes back with him. Then the punitive detachment comes to explain the arrangement to the village. Every one of those villages is recruiting for us now, and he has not worked out why.

My orders are the city and the western crossing, and to clear Plastunovskaya on the north road where his staff has installed itself. Anatoly is with the machine-gun company. He is twenty-two and he thinks that is very old.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Ekaterinodar (19,9), Ekaterinodar (20,13) and Elizabetinskaya (5,10).
- Take Plastunovskaya (25,1).

briliant.text:
The line held and Plastunovskaya is ours, with a staff car, a printing press and four sacks of their correspondence in the bargain.

It changes less than it should. Novorossiysk and the coast road are already lost, the railway to the north is cut in three places, and an army supplied by nothing but peasant carts cannot sit in a city with sixty thousand mouths in it. The Army Council has decided to go to Armavir and fight for the Terek instead. We leave in good order, on our own feet, with our guns - which after this summer is not nothing.

I have burned nothing and shot no one on the way out. Let them find the city as they find it, and let the people of Ekaterinodar compare.

intro:
The Taman Army

August 23rd, 1918

The Taman Group is cut off from the rest of the army by two hundred versts of White cavalry, with the sea on one side and the mountains on the other. There are thirty thousand people on the Novorossiysk road with it and perhaps a third of them carry a rifle; the rest are the families of the ones who do, and they know precisely what the punitive detachments do in the coastal stanitsas, because that is why they are on the road.

Kovtyukh has exactly one route - the coast road east through Gelendzhik - and there are German warships off the port to make sure he does not use the harbour instead.

His order to me is four words long: get the columns out. Not the ground. Not the town. Not the guns, if it comes to that.

Victory conditions:
- Bring eight of the ten marked Taman columns out through Gelendzhik (39,37).
- Or take the village at (41,3).
- You lose if not one marked column survives.

briliant.text:
Eight columns are through Gelendzhik and on the coast road, and the rearguard came out in order behind them with its machine guns still mounted.

The town is lost. It was lost before we started; a port under naval guns with no fleet of our own was never going to be held, and I said so at the council. What was in our hands was whether the Taman Army came out as an army or as a crowd on a road, and it has come out as an army.

They have five hundred versts of mountain track ahead of them to reach Armavir, and they will do it on foot, in August, eating what the stanitsas give them. When the history of this war is written that march will be in it.

intro:
Stavropol

November 10th, 1918

Denikin has drawn a ring round this army from the east, the west and the north, and is pressing it back against the mountains. Stavropol has already changed hands twice, and both times the change was paid for in whole regiments.

We are the 11th Army now, on paper, which has improved nothing. Sorokin, who commanded it, shot four members of the regional Party committee in October and was shot himself a fortnight later. The typhus is taking more of us than the shelling.

We hold the town and the villages that cover the road out of it. Wrangel is coming from the west, Drozdovsky from the north, and two batteries are ranging on us from ground I can see from the church tower. Hold the town, hold the road, and take those two villages away.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Stavropol (12,10), Novomaryevskaya (4,6), Tatarka (12,12) and Nadezhda (18,13).
- Take Dubovka (21,0) and Temnolesskaya (18,24).

briliant.text:
Stavropol is held, both battery positions are taken, and Drozdovsky was carried off the field with a wound that the doctors say he will not survive.

The 11th Army is still an army. That was the whole of my task and it is done.

It does not lift the ring. The Terek is being rolled up behind us and the typhus is taking more men than the Volunteers are; a front cannot be held by a garrison that cannot stand up. What we have bought is time and an intact road eastward, and both will be needed.

intro:
Grozny

February 1st, 1919

The Terek is the last thing we hold south of the Don and it is being taken away from us a stanitsa at a time. Grozny itself held for a hundred days last year - oilfield workers, Chechen and Ingush volunteers, a scratch garrison and no reserves at all - and the wells have been burning ever since. You can see them from thirty versts out; by now everyone here navigates by them.

What has changed is not on this map. The Great War ended in November, the Germans are gone from Ukraine, and the Entente has begun unloading at Novorossiysk for Denikin: British rifles, British shells, British instructors. Wrangel is already at Vladikavkaz.

The 12th Army holds Grozny, Shali and Samashki, and behind them there is nothing but the mountain passes. Hold the three towns. Take Novoshchendrinskaya, which is where their cavalry waters.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Grozny (21,23), Shali (33,27) and Samashki (7,31).
- Take Novoshchendrinskaya (31,5).

briliant.text:
The three towns are ours and their cavalry has been pushed off the river.

The 12th Army will still have to go over the passes. That was decided in Moscow and by the typhus, not here: with Vladikavkaz gone there is no front left to anchor on, and men who hold a town in an army that no longer exists are simply prisoners who have not been taken yet. We come out with our formations intact and our wounded with us.

The oil wells are burning again. We did not fire them; the retreating administration did, in 1918, and the Volunteers will say it was us. Let them.

intro:
The Manych

May 1st, 1919

The 10th Army came down off the Tsaritsyn line in the winter, took Torgovaya and put itself across the Manych, and for a few weeks it looked as though the southern front might be split in two. It has not happened. Wrangel has brought his Caucasus corps up by rail with British armour on the flat cars, and this steppe is flat, dry and belongs to whoever has the most horses - which is not us.

So it comes down to the crossings, and for once we are standing on ground we chose ourselves. Velikoknyazheskaya, Uyutnyy and Ekaterinovka cover the fords. Torgovaya, which we took in the winter, has been taken back, and I want it again.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Velikoknyazheskaya (40,13), Uyutnyy (34,14) and Ekaterinovka (23,23).
- Take Torgovaya (21,37).

briliant.text:
The fords are held and Torgovaya is ours again, with their forward dumps in it.

The 10th Army will nonetheless be pulling back over the Manych within the month. Not because of anything that happened on this ground: the Don Cossacks have risen behind our left at Veshenskaya, the 9th Army's flank has gone, and a bridgehead is only as good as the army standing behind it. We go back over the river as a formation, in our own time, with the crossings still in our hands - which is the difference between a withdrawal and a rout.

intro:
Tsaritsyn

June 14th, 1919

The Cossacks have come at this town three times since last summer and gone back three times with nothing, which is why the newspapers have started calling it the Red Verdun. What held it was not a miracle: the workers' regiments out of the French Factory, the armoured trains, the gunboats on the Volga, and a position that was dug and wired properly before anybody needed it. All of that is still here.

What is different is Wrangel, and the tanks the British landed for him at Novorossiysk, and the fact that our own front north of here has been coming apart since the Veshenskaya rising.

Hold the city, its approaches and the river crossing. Their heavy batteries have come into position at Gorodistsje; clear them off it.

Victory conditions:
- Hold the three Tsaritsyn sectors (22,13), (26,17), (14,21) and Wolzskij (37,10).
- Take Gorodistsje (4,12).

briliant.text:
The city is held, the crossing is open, and the battery position at Gorodistsje has been overrun with its guns still limbered.

The town will not stay ours for long, and everyone in this headquarters knows it. Denikin has issued what he is pleased to call the Moscow Directive; the whole southern front is moving, and Tsaritsyn is one anchor on a line that has already been turned in three other places. When we go, we will go with the army intact, the shops emptied and the barges upriver, and the men who held here will be needed at Orel.

There is a phrase going round the staff about the defence of last autumn - about the commissar from Moscow who requisitioned everything on the Volga and shot the specialists who argued. I have no orders to repeat it and no wish to. What held Tsaritsyn was the trenches and the men in them.

intro:
Oboyan

August 12th, 1919

Denikin signed his Moscow Directive last month in Tsaritsyn: three armies, three axes, one capital. May-Mayevsky's corps is coming up the Kharkov railway to deliver the middle of it, and Mamontov's cavalry is already somewhere behind us doing as it pleases in our rear areas - which is the part of the Directive that actually works.

The 13th Army has been ordered to hold the Oboyan-Pristen line long enough for the reserves forming at Orel and Tula to be worth something. That is a screen, and everyone from the army commander down has been careful to call it something else. There is no more to my task than that, and no less.

Break their forward group at Yakovlevo and buy the Republic three weeks.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Oboyan (22,7), Pristen (39,7), Trubezh (11,9) and the crossing at (9,1).
- Take Yakovlevo (26,27).

Intelligence: enemy cavalry has been reported in our rear areas. Expect to be raided.

briliant.text:
The line held for the whole of the allotted time and Yakovlevo was cleared on the last day. The reserves at Orel have their three weeks.

Kursk will still have to be given up. That is the army's decision and it is the right one: a screen that stays in place until it is surrounded has stopped being a screen. We go back on the Oboyan road in our own order, and the divisions that come out of here will be in the line at Orel when it matters.

One warning from the army: replacements will not be reaching us for some weeks. Count your losses before you take them.

lose.text:
The line broke at Trubezh on the fourth day and the cavalry in our rear did the rest. What reaches Kursk will not be fit to be called a division for a month.

The reserves at Orel will have to form up with the enemy already in front of them.

intro:
Peregonovka

September 26th, 1919

Makhno's people have been retreating west across half of Ukraine for a month with Slashchev's regiments driving them. This morning they stopped retreating: the whole Insurgent Army turned round in the dark near Peregonovka and went at the pursuit column head-on, and the tachanka squadrons are swinging wide to come in behind it.

I am attached to them as a liaison officer, which is a polite word for several things at once, and every one of them is somebody's problem for later. There is a great deal between us politically and there will be a reckoning over it.

Tonight none of that is the point. The group in front of us is Denikin's, it is sitting astride the railway to his rear at the exact moment his front line is reaching for Orel, and it can be destroyed. My formations remain the Red Army's, and so do I.

Victory conditions:
- Take Peregonovka (20,13).
- Or destroy 22 enemy formations.

briliant.text:
The pursuit group has been broken and ridden down. The tachankas came in across the stubble at first light and there was nowhere for the column to form square.

What follows matters more than the field. Denikin's rear in Ukraine is open, his supply trains from Berdyansk and Mariupol have to be found from somewhere else, and every regiment he sends back to deal with the insurgents is a regiment not marching on Moscow.

I have written up the action honestly, including who did the riding. There will be people at the front headquarters who will not want to read it that way.

The counterstroke failed. The Insurgent Army is off westward again and the railway to Denikin's rear is still his.

I am to rejoin the Southern Front. Nothing has been taken off the enemy's back and the whole weight of it is now coming north.

intro:
Orel: the avalanche

October 11th, 1919

Kutepov is coming up the Moscow highway with the Kornilov, Markov, Drozdovsky and Alekseyev regiments in his first line - four regiments of officers with nothing left to go home to, the best infantry the Whites have, and nobody has stopped them this summer. In front of them is the 13th Army, which has been retreating since August, and me.

We are not asked to stop them here. We are asked to hold Orel and the road towns long enough for the shock group forming behind Kromy - the Latvian Rifle Division, the Estonians, Primakov's Chervonny Cossacks - to come into line with its strength unspent. Eleven thousand bayonets that have not yet been in this battle, and every day this sector holds is a day they are still eleven thousand.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold four of the objectives for a brilliant victory, three for a victory, two for a tactical victory.
- Or take their forward depot at (41,27).
- The objectives are Orel (31,20), Mtsensk (33,9), Kromy (24,23) and Dmitrovsk (19,28).

briliant.text:
We held the line to the hour we were given, and the shock group at Kromy has come up complete: eleven thousand bayonets that have not yet been in this battle.

The high command has decided not to fight for the city itself with the troops already worn out on this ground. Orel may be given up for a few days if the shock group is thereby put in on the flank instead of being fed into the front. That is not a defeat of ours; it is what the last week was bought for.

Latyshi are already moving into position west of Kromy. The counterstroke goes in this week.

The line went in the middle and the road towns with it. The shock group has had to be committed early and piecemeal to cover the retreat, which is exactly what it was assembled not to do.

Kutepov is on the Tula road. What is left of this army is going back with him behind it.

intro:
Orel: the storm

October 16th, 1919

Comrades of the shock group.

Five days ago their newspapers in Kharkov printed the distance from Orel to Moscow. They were right about the distance and wrong about everything else.

That corps has been marching and fighting for eleven weeks without a reserve, on a front that gets wider with every verst it advances. Makhno is across its supply line. Its regiments are officers, and officers cannot be replaced out of the villages it has just requisitioned - those villages are recruiting for us. It is a spear thrown a very long way by an arm that is now behind it.

You are the Latvian Rifle Division, the Estonian division and the Chervonny Cossacks, and you are going in on the flank at Kromy, where the corps is thinnest and where its line of retreat runs. Take Orel back. Take Kromy and Dmitrovsk. Do not let them straighten the front.

Victory conditions:
- Take Orel (31,20), Kromy (24,23) and Dmitrovsk (19,28).
- Hold Mtsensk (33,9) and Karachev (19,13).

briliant.text:
Orel is ours. Kromy is ours. The Kornilov regiment left its wounded in the school at Dmitrovsk and went south in the dark.

This is the turn of the whole war and it should be written down as such while the ground is still warm. From here the Southern Front does not defend; it advances. Kursk, then Kharkov, then the Donbass, and then the sea.

The Latvian regiments lost heavily in the wood north of Kromy. Their commander asked that the divisional order should name the companies rather than the division. It will.

lose.text:

The road to Tula is open and the reserves that were to have won this battle have been spent fighting it.

intro:
Tula

November 3rd, 1919

Tula makes the rifles. That sentence is the whole of the situation, and it is why I am here and not anywhere else.

Their advanced parties are at Plavsk, thirty versts down the road. Against them: the workers' regiments of the arms works, a fortified belt that the townspeople dug themselves through October, and six divisions brought in from the Voronezh and Tsaritsyn sectors - which the enemy has kindly made possible by concentrating everything against this one town and leaving his own left flank standing in the air.

Hold the belt. And if the chance offers, take Plavsk off them and their staging point with it.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold four of the objectives for a brilliant victory, three for a victory, two for a tactical victory.
- Or take Plavsk (4,36).
- The objectives are Tula (13,13), Bronnokovo (28,12), Novomoskovsk (31,22) and Bogoroditsk (30,34).

briliant.text:
The belt held and the arms works never stopped. Sixty thousand rifles went out of this town while the fighting was inside artillery range of it.

That is the end of their northern effort. Their left has been stripped bare to make this attack and Budyonny's cavalry is already through the gap at Kastornoye. We are going back onto the Kharkov line - forward, at last, and on our own initiative.

lose.text:
The belt was forced south-east of the town. The works are being evacuated by rail under fire and the machinery that cannot be moved is being broken up.

The road north is open. There is one line left in front of Moscow and we are it.

intro:
Moscow

December 12th, 1919

I did not expect to write this heading.

Their cavalry is in the outer suburbs. The Council of Defence has not left. The Kremlin garrison is in the line like everybody else, and the barricades on the southern approaches were thrown up by people who came out of the factories carrying their own tools.

We hold the three southern sectors and the centre. Volkhonka, on the Kaluga road, is where their staff and their heavy batteries have come up; take it and the whole attack loses its hinge. There is no line behind this one, which simplifies the orders considerably.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold four of the objectives for a brilliant victory, three for a victory, two for a tactical victory.
- Or take Volkhonka (24,35).
- The objectives are the three Moscow sectors (18,14), (36,17), (12,19) and Red Square (24,20).

briliant.text:
The city is held. The attack has stopped at the barricades and gone no further, and this morning their forward regiments were seen going back down the Kaluga road with their guns.

They cannot stay where they are. Their army is four hundred versts from a railhead it still holds, in December, with the Don rising behind it and the Ukrainian rear in insurgent hands. What broke here was not just an assault but the whole idea of the march on Moscow.

The front headquarters wants me back in the south for the pursuit. I am to go by the first train.

lose.text:
The southern sectors were lost house by house and the centre is under direct fire. The Council of Defence has moved. The fighting goes on in the streets and will go on in them.

I am ordered north tonight, to Petrograd, where the last formed reserve of the Republic is. I do not want to go and I am going.

intro:
Petrograd

January 26th, 1920

I am detached from the Southern Front and placed under the 7th Army. My opponent is no longer Denikin but Yudenich - the North-Western Army, fed and armed out of Reval, with British tanks and British naval guns off Kronstadt, making one more winter push at the city while there is still enough of it left to push at.

Petrograd has been stripped for every other front for two years. What is here is the workers' regiments, the sailors, the courses cadets and whatever the districts can still put in the line. We hold the four city sectors and the airfield. Their road in - and their road out - runs through the Moscow highway junction.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold five of the objectives for a brilliant victory, four for a victory, three for a tactical victory.
- Or take the Moscow Road junction (34,33).
- The objectives are the four Petrograd sectors (16,12), (22,12), (14,15), (18,15) and the airfield (24,20).

briliant.text:
The city is held and the North-Western Army has come apart in front of it. Their formations are going back over the Estonian border to be disarmed and interned by the government they were fighting for.

It is over on this front, and it ended the way this whole war seems to end things: not with a surrender but with an army walking off the map. Peace talks with Estonia begin at Tartu within days.

I am recalled to the Southern Front. Kharkov is the next name in my orders.

They are in the outskirts and the fighting is in the Petrograd streets. There is nothing further back to send and nothing further back to go to.

This is the end of it. Whatever is written afterwards, it was not for want of men who stood where they were told to stand.

intro:
Kharkov

December 4th, 1919

Since Orel this front has not stopped. Kursk went in the middle of November. Budyonny's cavalry is cutting the Donets railway in three places at once. The Volunteer Army that was going to be in Moscow by Christmas is trying to hold a line it does not have the men for, and it is finding out what its own rear is worth: the districts it requisitioned all summer are not sending it a single recruit. We are the ones advancing now, and it has taken some getting used to.

Kharkov is the hinge. Take the three city sectors and the whole Donbass position goes with them; leave it and their army has somewhere to reform. There is not much time - their rearguard is fighting for days, not for ground.

Victory conditions:
- Take the three Kharkov sectors (21,16), (14,18) and (15,21) - fast. Six turns for a brilliant victory, nine for a victory, twelve at the outside.
- Hold Lyubotyn (3,14) and the crossing at (24,8).

briliant.text:
Kharkov is ours with its workshops, its rolling stock and eleven locomotives that were still under steam. Their rearguard did not have the time it wanted.

Their army is splitting in two: one part towards Rostov and the Kuban, the other towards the Crimea. Once that has happened it cannot be undone, and neither half can support the other. The pursuit goes on to the sea.

We took the city, but slowly, and slow was the one thing that mattered here. Their rearguard held the crossings the extra four days it needed and their staff and depots are out along the Rostov line.

They will be able to reform on the Don. We shall have to fight for that too.

intro:
Novorossiysk

March 12th, 1920

The Kuban has gone. Rostov has gone. Ekaterinodar went last week. Everything left of them in the south is trying to get into the last port they hold on this coast, and the roads down to the harbour are one continuous column of transport.

In the roadstead there are British and French warships and nothing like enough transports. Their command has drawn up a list of who is taken off and who is not, and the men who are not have begun to work that out for themselves. Two years of Entente supply comes down to the tonnage in that bay this week.

Our task is the harbour and the loading. Take the port and the evacuation stops; break up the columns at the moles and it stops anyway. Six marked columns are what the whole affair now turns on.

Victory conditions:
- Take the Novorossiysk port (16,14).
- Or destroy 18 enemy formations.
- The enemy also loses if four of his six marked evacuation columns are destroyed.

briliant.text:
The port is ours. What was still on the quays when our cavalry came down the hill went into captivity where it stood - twenty-two thousand men, the horses, the guns, and the stores the ships had no room for.

Part of the army got away to the Crimea. That was decided in the roadstead by the tonnage available and not on this ground. What did not get away was the Armed Forces of South Russia as a field army; Denikin resigned command within the fortnight.

Wrangel has taken over what reached Sevastopol. There is one more campaign in this.

The embarkation went on to the end and the transports sailed full. We came down to a quay of abandoned horses and burning stores.

Everything that got onto those ships will be facing us again in the Crimea, and it will have British guns when it does.

intro:
Perekop

November 7th, 1920

Wrangel has spent a summer turning the isthmus into a fortress: the Turkish Wall across the neck at Perekop, the Yushun positions behind it, eight belts of wire, concrete emplacements and every gun the French landed at Sevastopol. He has said publicly that it cannot be taken. Several of our own specialists have said the same thing rather more quietly.

So we are not going to take it the way he has built it to be taken. The front attacks frontally at Perekop and, on the same night, crosses the Sivash - which is shallow, freezing, and with this wind fordable. The 15th and 52nd divisions and the Latvian riflemen go across the mud in the dark; Blyukher's 51st goes at the Wall.

Take Armyansk and the wall positions, then Krasnoperekopsk and Zalivnaye behind them. Three years to the day since the Revolution, and the last of them is behind this wall.

Victory conditions:
- Take Krasnoperekopsk (40,34) and Zalivnaye (27,36).
- Hold Armyansk (21,12) and the two flanking positions (28,7) and (4,18).

briliant.text:
The Wall is taken and the Yushun positions behind it are taken. The columns that went across the Sivash came out of the mud on the far shore at four in the morning, into the flank of the whole position, and after that the fortress that could not be taken was a line of concrete with nobody behind it.

Wrangel is embarking at Sevastopol, Yalta and Feodosiya. He is doing it well - better than Novorossiysk, and there are ships for everyone who reaches the quays. A hundred and fifty thousand people are leaving Russia and most of them will not come back.

The war in the south is over. I am forty-one years old, I have served two Russias, and I am going to write to Katya that she can come home.
